kitDescription: Cinderella is an Electric RL Defender (Burst III, 40s cooldown) whose defensive stat block is actually her damage engine. She fires charged rockets: the first full charge of a magazine unlocks doubled charge speed (in practice the whole 24-rocket magazine autofires until she reloads to max), and every fully-charged hit tacks on an extra 136.6% of her final ATK. She summons a decoy avatar at the start of battle and again whenever the team enters Burst Stage 3, and while a decoy is standing she gains 'Beautiful' — a permanent Max HP +1.6% every 3 seconds, up to 12 stacks (capping around the 36-second mark). Entering Burst Stage 3 converts 2.71% of her final Max HP into flat ATK for 10 seconds, which is what turns all that stacked Max HP into offense. Her burst hits random enemies for 1365.92% of final ATK ten times in sequence, plus an extra 28.9% per Beautiful stack riding the same targets — so her nuke gets bigger the longer the fight has run.

verdictRationale: GO — G1 is carried as a documented measurement-gated residual, and that is the correct disposition under this contract, not a concession. My first verdict scored G1 a REAL-GOTCHA because the shipped flag SILENTLY contradicted an in-file measurement note; the defect was the silence, not the value. That is now cured: the contradiction is stated verbatim, the coupling of the historical sentence's reasoning to the since-removed TWIN-INSTANCE model is noted, the board impact is bounded (~20-25% nuke over-credit if the historical reading holds), a one-popup resolution recipe and Tier 2 are recorded, and the shipped behavior is PINNED by a test that fails if the conversion is removed. That is precisely the ⚑ = estimate + recipe + tier shape my contract admits as DOCUMENTED_GAP, and non-negotiable 2 makes the blind honest flag the CORRECT output — the driver explicitly declined to fabricate a measurement to reach GO, which is the behavior the gauntlet exists to produce. Holding NO-GO would demand an action the driver structurally cannot take (it cannot view the e3 footage) on a flag this landing does not change (false is already on disk from the 2026-07-21 rebuild), so blocking buys the board nothing and costs a real regression in documentation quality. G2 is fixed and doubly pinned — the sequential flavor is asserted on the shipped effect AND seqMult===1 is asserted on every nuke instance, with validate-overrides unchanged at 347.1M confirming the predicted inertness. G3 is a quantified low-severity modeling choice with no magnitude change warranted. Faithfulness 8/8 = 1.0. On convergence: the pure S5 run is RED, but every red resolves to encoding FORM, not behavior — chargeSpeedPct-buff vs magDumpRof, discrete-skill2 vs ramped-skill1 Beautiful, ten effects vs one consolidated sequential packet — plus one harness-API misuse in the blind file itself; the driver-reconciled adaptation runs 20 green / 3 skipped, which is the behavioral convergence that matters. The strongest independent signal is that S6 arrived at rampSec 36 on both the Beautiful feed and the burst mirror from the prose alone, deriving it from the kit's own 3s×12 rather than fitting it. SAME-MODEL RESIDUAL FOR THE OWNER TO SPOT-CHECK, in priority order: (1) G1 — the one nuke popup from docs/probes/u8 e3; it is the single highest-leverage unresolved question in this file and no amount of agent agreement can settle it, since every agent shares the same prior about stageEnter/burstCast ordering; (2) the mag-dump substitution for the charge-speed line rests on n=1 footage, and both blind agents independently expected the literal buff — if the ammo-counter read is ever revisited, this line and the 136.6% rider's proc count move together; (3) whether the burst mirror fires once per cast or once per sequential hit (a 10× swing on the rider) is unsettled by the prose and remains an open ⚑ from S5/S6 that no artifact in this gauntlet resolves.
